text:
maya (frontend): FYI seeing huge spikes in interactiveFrameTime95 for the multi-series 'customer-compare' dashboard after yesterday's routing policy change. Charts freeze for ~700-1500ms intermittently on load.

allison (eng-platform): Ugh, saw that metric too. Correlates with an increase in chunk fetches per session (chunk_retrieval_count up ~3x).

maya (frontend): The baffling bit: it only repros when you have >6 series and the metrics come from mixed regions. local dev can't repro reliably.

samir (sre): Rollout-bucket was moved to affinity-by-route for that customer cohort right? Could be we split users across chunk-versions and invalidate cache often.

allison (eng-platform): Correct — we switched routing.policy -> "affinity by route" to reduce cross-region tails. Suspect side-effect: the client chunk key includes route-specific seed which changes on affinity fallback. That causes repeated rehydration downloads.

maya (frontend): Confirmed in devtools: same chunk filename but query param differs: `?route_affinity=v2-04` vs `?route_affinity=v1`. When they differ the service returns 302 -> new signed URL and the browser doesn't reuse the cache entry.

samir (sre): 302s are cheap but cause extra RTT + main-thread parse. For 10+ chunks that adds up. Any quick mitigation?

allison (eng-platform): Two options: 1) strip route_affinity from chunk payload url (server rewrite) or 2) introduce client-side soft-ttl + in-memory dedupe so parallel downloads for same logical chunk dedupe for N ms.

maya (frontend): 1) feels risky mid-rollout — might undo affinity guarantees. 2) sounds safer: keep cache key but coalesce fetches. We already have a small dedupe util, but it doesn't handle query-params mismatch. Could add a logical-chunk-id header from runtime.

samir (sre): If we add logical-chunk-id we need to ensure signed URL generation includes it and canonicalizes the cache key. That's infra change. How fast can infra do it?

dmitri (infra): I can add a canonical X-RW-Chunk-ID header on the edge signed-url service. It'd be a low-risk change: the signed url will still vary but we'd emit the header and a small edge rule to set Cache-Key = X-RW-Chunk-ID for CDN. Rolling in ~2 days with canary.

maya (frontend): Nice. Meanwhile can we deploy a client fallback: if fetch count > 1 for same chunkName within 500ms, reuse the in-flight promise? I'll prototype now.

allison (eng-platform): Also let's monitor a couple metrics in the canary: interactiveFrameTime95, chunk_retrieval_count, chunk_dup_fetch_rate (new metric), and session_cold_start_rate. Rollout-bot: create canary with 5% + alert if interFrameTime95 > baseline * 1.3 for 10m.

rollout-bot: Canary created: env=canary, pct=5, alert=interactiveFrameTime95 > 1.3x baseline for 10m. Link: https://rollouts.internal/canary/1732

samir (sre): One more thought — telemetry sampling was at 1% on that dashboard route, so the signal was noisy. Bumping telemetry to 5% for the canary will give us clearer correlations.

allison (eng-platform): Agreed. I'll bump telemetry sampling for routes affected and add a quick integration test that simulates mixed-region series to catch rehydration thrash in PR checks.

maya (frontend): Prototype pushed: dedupe-layer handles name-mapped ids, and adds a soft-ttl of 800ms for revalidation. If infra X-RW-Chunk-ID lands we switch to header-based canonicalization. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/frontend/pulls/1182

dmitri (infra): Noted. I'll queue the edge change — preview in staging next 6h. Need a small config: `edge.cacheKey: useHeader X-RW-Chunk-ID if present`.

samir (sre): After infra change, let's run the canary and watch chunk_dup_fetch_rate and interactiveFrameTime95. If dedupe + header reduces dup fetches by >90% and interFrameTime95 drops ~30-50% we can promote.

maya (frontend): Also adding a tiny telemetry ping from the chunk loader: `chunk_load_path` with values [cache-hit, canonical-miss, deduped-inflight, network-fresh]. That'll help disambiguate.

allison (eng-platform): Good. Action items: dmitri - edge header rule + canary; maya - client dedupe PR; samir - bump telemetry sampling; rollout-bot - monitor and alert. Ship plan in PR comments.

maya (frontend): tl;dr: probable cause = query-param route affinity causing cache fragmentation -> extra 302s + parse + rehydration. Mitigation = client dedupe + edge canonical header before route sweep.

samir (sre): 👍 prioritize canary metric window. If we see any error spike revert client change — small risk of blocking chunk loads if bug.

allison (eng-platform): I'll update the incident doc if things regress: /incidents/console-chunk-oscillation.md (short note).

maya (frontend): Thanks all. I'll ping again once dedupe PR is green on staging and we have first canary numbers. :rocket:
